lines.cap: They were the richest family in America. A century later, at their family reunion, not one of the hundred and twenty was a millionaire.
lines.say: They were the richest family in America. A century later, at their family reunion, not one of the hundred and twenty was a millionaire.

lines.cap: Cornelius Vanderbilt. Ferries, then railroads. When he died in 1877, he had about a hundred million dollars. More than the US Treasury held.
lines.say: Cornelius Vanderbilt. Ferries, then railroads. When he died in 1877, he had about a hundred million dollars. More than the US Treasury held.

lines.cap: His son doubled it, in just eight years.
lines.say: His son doubled it, in just eight years.

lines.cap: Then the grandkids got the money. And they spent it like a competition.
lines.say: Then the grandkids got the money. And they spent it like a competition.

lines.cap: The Breakers. A seventy room summer house. Biltmore. A two hundred and fifty room house, still the biggest home in America.
lines.say: The Breakers. A seventy room summer house. Biltmore. A two hundred and fifty room house, still the biggest home in America.

lines.cap: Parties where guests dug for jewels in sandboxes. A ball that cost millions in today's money.
lines.say: Parties where guests dug for jewels in sandboxes. A ball that cost millions in today's money.

lines.cap: Nobody built anything new. The money just poured out. By 1973, at a family reunion at Vanderbilt University, not one of the hundred and twenty relatives was a millionaire.
lines.say: Nobody built anything new. The money just poured out. By 1973, at a family reunion at Vanderbilt University, not one of the hundred and twenty relatives was a millionaire.
